content.user_title: Design Reliable REST and GraphQL APIs
content.value_statement: Poor API contracts slow delivery and create inconsistent client behavior. This skill gives teams practical REST and GraphQL patterns, review checklists, and implementation guidance.
actual_capabilities: Reviews REST resource naming, HTTP method use, status codes, pagination, filtering, and error responses.
Guides GraphQL schema design for types, queries, mutations, subscriptions, pagination, and deprecation.
Provides an API design checklist covering auth, rate limits, testing, documentation, security, and monitoring.
Includes a FastAPI REST template with models, pagination, validation, error handling, and middleware examples.
Explains implementation patterns for versioning, caching, HATEOAS, DataLoader batching, and N+1 query prevention.
limitations: It gives design guidance and examples, not a complete production implementation for every framework.
Example code needs environment-specific security, persistence, authentication, and deployment configuration.
It cannot validate live API behavior unless you provide specifications, examples, or implementation details.
It does not replace security review for sensitive data flows, access control, or compliance requirements.

use_cases.title: Review a REST API before implementation
use_cases.description: Check resource naming, methods, pagination, versioning, errors, authentication, and documentation before engineers start building.

use_cases.title: Shape a GraphQL schema for a product domain
use_cases.description: Define types, inputs, payloads, pagination, error patterns, and DataLoader usage for a maintainable schema.

use_cases.title: Create shared API design standards
use_cases.description: Turn REST and GraphQL conventions into a practical checklist for reviews, onboarding, and governance.

prompt_templates.title: Review Basic REST Endpoints
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of an endpoint list.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my REST endpoint list for resource naming, HTTP methods, status codes, pagination, and error handling. Explain the highest priority changes first.

prompt_templates.title: Design a GraphQL Schema
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate schema planning for a new domain.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me design a GraphQL schema for [domain]. Include core types, queries, mutations, pagination, errors, and deprecation guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Create API Standards
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft team API design standards for REST and GraphQL services. Cover naming, auth, versioning, documentation, testing, and review gates.

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate Migration Tradeoffs
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess whether our product should move from REST to GraphQL. Compare consumer needs, cache behavior, operational risk, rollout strategy, and governance.

output_examples.input: A team asks for feedback on a new user management REST API.
output: Resource names become consistent plural nouns across collections.
Create, update, and delete operations use the expected HTTP method semantics.
Pagination, validation errors, and authentication failures receive explicit response patterns.

output_examples.input: A product team needs a GraphQL schema for posts, comments, and authors.
output: The schema separates object types, input types, mutation payloads, and error results.
Cursor pagination is recommended for large lists and changing feeds.
Resolver guidance includes DataLoader batching to avoid repeated data fetches.

output_examples.input: An engineering lead wants a reusable API review checklist.
output: The checklist covers resource design, status codes, versioning, auth, rate limits, testing, and documentation.
GraphQL-specific checks cover schema shape, mutation payloads, query limits, and deprecation.
Reviewers get concrete acceptance criteria before implementation begins.

best_practices: Start with consumers, use cases, and lifecycle constraints before choosing REST or GraphQL.
Define errors, pagination, authentication, versioning, and documentation before implementation starts.
Review examples against the checklist and adapt templates to each production environment.
anti_patterns: Using action-oriented endpoint names when resource-oriented names would be clearer.
Copying example middleware or server settings without production-specific security configuration.
Adding GraphQL fields or REST versions without a deprecation and migration plan.

faq.question: Does this skill write production API code?
faq.answer: It includes examples and templates, but users must adapt security, storage, auth, and deployment details.

faq.question: Can it review existing OpenAPI specs?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide the relevant endpoints, schemas, or spec excerpts for design-focused feedback.

faq.question: Does it support both REST and GraphQL?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers REST resources and GraphQL schema patterns in separate reference guides.

faq.question: Can it help choose REST or GraphQL?
faq.answer: Yes. It can compare client needs, caching, operational complexity, governance, and migration risk.

faq.question: Does it handle authentication design?
faq.answer: It covers auth strategy, status codes, error semantics, and rate limits at the API design level.

faq.question: Is it tied to one framework?
faq.answer: No. The FastAPI sample is illustrative, while most guidance applies across languages and frameworks.
